spec.title: codexlb2otel - Full Telemetry
spec.description: Every signal codexlb2otel emits: all 57 metrics, all 9 Loki record types, and the trace tree. Ten tabs, from agent behaviour through to the exporter's own health. Generated by dashboards/v2/generate.py, which fails the build if any declared metric or record type loses its last panel.

spec.name: model
spec.label: Model
spec.description: Filters every panel whose metric carries gen_ai_request_model. Metrics without that label (the selfobs family) deliberately ignore it.

spec.name: account
spec.label: Account
spec.description: Grafana Cloud-style account id from the archive. Rate limits and credits are per account.

spec.name: kind
spec.label: Request kind
spec.description: turn, prewarm, compaction, memory. These run CONCURRENTLY on one thread - filtering to turn hides real spend.

spec.name: record_type
spec.label: Log record type
spec.description: Loki stream label. One of nine record kinds.

spec.name: family
spec.label: Transport family
spec.description: Loki stream label: websocket or unknown.

spec.name: search
spec.label: Log search
spec.description: Case-insensitive regex applied to log line content on the Conversation Logs tab. Leave as . to match everything.

options.content:
**Metric timestamps are INGEST time, not event time.** The exporter tails an archive and records into
the OTel SDK as it reads, so replaying a backlog - after a restart, or on first deployment - lands hours
of traffic on a few minutes of wall clock. A tall narrow spike across every panel at the same instant is
that, not a traffic surge. Cross-check against **ingest lag**: if it was high and falling at that moment,
you are looking at catch-up.

The **logs** do not have this problem (they carry the record's own timestamp, and anything older than
3h is dropped rather than backdated), and neither do the **traces**. Only the metrics.

`request_kind` - turn, prewarm, compaction, memory - are **concurrent series on one thread**, not phases
of one another. Filtering to `turn` hides real spend.

spec.title: Ingest lag
spec.description: Wall clock now minus the newest record timestamp the tailer has seen. The one number that tells you whether anything else on this dashboard is current. Healthy is roughly the poll interval (5s). This is the ONLY wall-clock subtraction anywhere in the pipeline - everything else is measured against the archive's own clock.

spec.title: Turns
spec.description: Logical turns completed in the selected range. A turn is the whole user-visible exchange; a response is one model call within it.

spec.title: Responses
spec.description: Model responses in range. Responses per turn above ~1 means the harness is looping - tool calls, retries, or continuation.

spec.title: Tokens
spec.description: input + output ONLY. Summing every gen_ai.token.type would double-count: cache_read is a sub-bucket nested inside input, and reasoning inside output, not additive siblings of them. See the Tokens tab.

spec.title: Errors
spec.description: Error events in range, from the archive's own error records - not this exporter's health. Zero is the expected value.

spec.title: Rate-limit headroom (worst account)
spec.description: 100 minus the highest primary-window utilisation across accounts. This is the number that decides whether the next request gets served.

spec.title: Turn and response rate
spec.description: Three levels of the same traffic: turns (user-visible), responses (model calls), engine calls (upstream inference invocations). The gaps between them are where tool loops and retries live.

spec.title: Turn duration percentiles
spec.description: End-to-end logical turn latency by model. Decomposed on the Latency tab.

spec.title: Token rate (additive: input + output)
spec.description: Only input and output are stacked, because only they are additive. cache_read and reasoning are breakdowns NESTED inside them and appear on the Tokens tab, unstacked - stacking a sub-bucket on its parent silently doubles the total.

spec.title: Traffic by model
spec.description: Which model is actually doing the work.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__range]))

spec.title: Pipeline and sink health
spec.description: Steady values are healthy. Open responses climbing without bound means completion frames are not arriving and the reducer is accumulating.

spec.title: Log volume by record type
spec.description: Every line this exporter pushes to Loki, by kind. Backlog older than loki.max_line_age (3h) is dropped locally rather than silently discarded server-side, so a gap here during catch-up is expected, not a fault.

spec.title: Responses by status
spec.description: completed is the happy path. Anything else is worth a look on the Errors tab.

spec.title: Responses by request kind
spec.description: turn, prewarm, compaction and memory run CONCURRENTLY on the same thread - they are separate metric series, not phases of one another. Prewarm and compaction volume is invisible to the user but not to the bill.

spec.title: Turns by originator and thread source
spec.description: Which client produced the traffic and how the thread began.

spec.title: Response outcome matrix
spec.description: The three labels that matter, crossed. Read it as: which model, doing what, ended how.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_status, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Reasoning level and service tier
spec.description: Reasoning level drives both latency and reasoning-token spend; service tier drives queueing.

spec.title: Request vs response model (substitution)
spec.description: These differ when the service substitutes a model. A row where they do not match is not an error, but it changes what you are actually paying for and what latency to expect.

spec.title: Baseline resets
spec.description: A cumulative counter on a thread went backwards, so the reducer rebased it. Expected at thread start and after a reconnect; a sustained rate means sequence tracking is losing frames and per-response deltas may be wrong.

spec.title: Attributes rejected by the cardinality guard
spec.description: One guard per process caps distinct values per attribute. A non-zero rate means real values are being dropped to protect cardinality - the metric is still correct in aggregate but a dimension has gone lossy. Investigate before raising the cap.

spec.title: Recent turn records
spec.description: One line per completed logical turn, carrying the full structured metadata set - thread, session, window, account, plan, token usage. Expand a line to pivot into any of it.

spec.title: gen_ai.token.type is NOT a flat enum

options.content:
`input` and `output` are additive siblings. **`cache_read` is nested inside `input`** and **`reasoning`
is nested inside `output`** - they are breakdowns of their parent, not peers of it. Summing or stacking
all four double-counts, which is why the panels below keep the additive view and the nested view apart,
and why the ratio panel divides `cache_read` by `input` rather than by `input + cache_read`.

That nesting is also what `gen_ai_token_semantics="inclusive"` declares on these series, so a consumer
never has to infer it from the provider name.

The same trap is why `engine_uncached_prompt_tokens` is deliberately a separate metric rather than a
fifth `gen_ai.token.type` value: `uncached = input - cache_read` is another nested breakdown, and putting
it on the same axis would double-count against `input` for anyone who did not know to exclude it.

spec.title: Additive token volume (input + output)
spec.description: Safe to stack: these two do not overlap, so the stack height is the real total.

spec.title: Nested breakdowns (cache_read within input, reasoning within output)
spec.description: Deliberately NOT stacked. Each line is a subset of one of the lines in the panel above, so stacking them together would be arithmetically meaningless.

spec.title: Cache read ratio
spec.description: cache_read / input. The denominator is input alone, NOT input + cache_read, because cache_read is already counted inside input - dividing by the sum would understate the hit rate and can never reach 100%. This is the single biggest lever on spend, and it collapses whenever the prompt prefix changes: a system-prompt edit shows up here before it shows up on the bill.

spec.expr: 100 * sum(rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", gen_ai_token_type="cache_read"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", gen_ai_token_type="input"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

spec.title: Uncached prompt tokens
spec.description: The engine's own count of prompt tokens it had to process rather than reuse. Cross-check against the cache ratio above: they should move inversely.

spec.title: Token usage distribution (gen_ai semconv)
spec.description: The OTel GenAI standard histogram, kept alongside the codexlb counter deliberately: this one is per-request DISTRIBUTION, the counter is volume. A rising p99 with flat volume is prompt growth.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Tokens by model and kind
spec.description: Where the tokens actually went. Sort by value to find the expensive corner - it is often compaction or prewarm rather than user turns.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind, gen_ai_token_type) (increase(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Image generation tokens
spec.description: NO DATA IS THE EXPECTED STATE on this capture - no image generation has occurred. The panel exists so the first image-generating turn is visible immediately rather than being invisible until someone thinks to look.

spec.title: Web search requests
spec.description: Also expected empty on this capture. Web search is billed separately from tokens, so it is worth its own panel rather than being folded into tool calls.

spec.title: Credits balance
spec.description: Remaining credit, per account. Flat at zero with unlimited=1 below is a plan without a balance, not an exhausted one.

spec.title: Unlimited plan
spec.description: 1 when the account's plan carries no credit limit. Reads the credits balance above for you - a zero balance means nothing on an unlimited plan.

options.content:
The critical path decomposes one response into **pre-inference → engine wall → sampling and stream**,
plus whatever is left over. Each stage is a histogram in its own right, so a slow turn can be attributed
rather than guessed at. `critical_path_coverage` on the stage metrics tells you whether the stages
actually account for the whole response - when it says partial, the decomposition is missing a piece and
the leftovers land in *other*.

The `engine_*` family is the upstream provider's own timing, reported back in the frames: **service**
timings are what the serving layer measured, **iapi** timings are what the inner inference API measured.
`service_minus_iapi_tbt` is the gap between them - queueing and transport that belongs to neither model.

The `responses_excl_*` family is the same response measured with different things subtracted, so you can
isolate what a stage costs by comparing two of them rather than trusting a single attribution.

spec.title: Critical path stages (p95)
spec.description: Stacked p95 by stage. Stacking quantiles is not arithmetically exact - p95s do not sum - but it is the fastest way to see WHICH stage moved, which is the question this panel exists to answer. Use the mean panel below when you need the sum to be honest.

spec.title: Critical path stages (mean, additive)
spec.description: Means DO sum, so this stack is a true decomposition. Split by critical_path_coverage so a partial attribution cannot masquerade as a complete one.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_pre_inference_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_pre_inference_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_engine_wall_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_engine_wall_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_sampling_and_stream_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (codexlb_critical_path_coverage) (rate(codexlb_sampling_and_stream_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

spec.title: Engine wall by model
spec.description: Time the upstream engine was working, as it reported it. This is the part no amount of local tuning changes.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_wall_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_wall_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_wall_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Service vs IAPI inference
spec.description: Two measurements of the same inference from different layers. A widening gap is overhead between them, not a slower model.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_inference_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_inference_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_inference_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_iapi_inference_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Service vs IAPI sampling
spec.description: Same pairing for the sampling phase - generating tokens once the prompt is processed.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_sampling_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_sampling_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_sampling_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_iapi_sampling_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Time between tokens
spec.description: TBT is what streaming feels like. The service-minus-iapi gap is transport and queueing between the two layers - if that is what is large, the model is not the problem.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_tbt_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_tbt_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_tbt_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_iapi_tbt_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_engine_service_minus_iapi_tbt_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Time to first token (gen_ai semconv)
spec.description: TTFT dominates perceived responsiveness far more than total duration does.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Response duration, with stages excluded
spec.description: The same response with different components subtracted. Differences between these lines ARE the components - this is how you attribute latency without trusting a single computed breakdown.

spec.title: gen_ai client operation duration (by status)
spec.description: The OTel GenAI standard latency histogram, split by outcome. Errors that are FAST and errors that are SLOW are different failures.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, status) (rate(gen_ai_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, status) (rate(gen_ai_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, status) (rate(gen_ai_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Engine wall heatmap
spec.description: The distribution rather than its summary. Bimodality - two bands - means two populations of request, which a p95 line hides completely. A single narrow vertical band is the backlog-replay artifact described on the Overview tab, not a real burst: every bucket was filled during one catch-up pass.

spec.title: Client tool pause
spec.description: Time the model spent waiting on a CLIENT-side tool - the harness, not the provider. Expected empty on this capture. When it is not empty, this is latency you own and can actually fix.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_client_tool_pause_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Tool call rate by tool
spec.description: Which tools the agent actually reaches for.

spec.title: Tool calls in range
spec.description: Same data ranked. The long tail is usually more interesting than the head.

spec.title: Tool calls per operation
spec.description: How many tools one response invokes. A rising p99 is an agent looping - it costs tokens and latency without necessarily failing, so nothing else alerts.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_tool_calls_per_operation_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_tool_calls_per_operation_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_tool_calls_per_operation_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Tool call records
spec.description: Individual tool invocations with arguments, bounded at 16KB per call. Truncation is marked inline with the original length.

spec.title: Tool output records
spec.description: What came back. Paired with the call above by turn and thread id.

spec.title: Subagent activity
spec.description: Turns attributable to a subagent rather than the top-level thread. Only the instructions record carries subagent lineage, which is why this is derived from turns rather than counted directly.

spec.title: Instructions records (agent lineage)
spec.description: The only record carrying parent_thread_id, parent_turn_id, forked_from_thread_id and subagent_kind - the agent tree lives here. instructions_hash lets you tell a prompt change from a prompt reuse.

spec.title: Agent messages
spec.description: What the agent said, as opposed to what it did.

spec.title: Primary window utilisation
spec.description: Percent of the account's primary rate-limit window consumed. This is reported BY the provider in the frames, not inferred here.

spec.title: Per-model window utilisation
spec.description: Some models carry their own window. This one can be exhausted while the primary window above still looks healthy - that mismatch is exactly the case worth watching.

spec.title: Time until window reset
spec.description: Sawtooth is healthy - it should fall to zero and jump back. A flat line means the value has stopped being refreshed and everything above it is stale.

spec.title: Current utilisation
spec.description: At-a-glance headroom per account.

spec.title: Traffic by plan type and service tier
spec.description: Plan governs the limits; tier governs the queue. Both change what a given latency number means.

spec.title: Engine calls by account
spec.description: Upstream invocations attributed to each account - the thing the rate limits above are actually counting.

spec.title: Error rate by type and code
spec.description: Errors carried in the archive - the provider's and the harness's, not this exporter's. For the exporter's own health use the Pipeline tab.

spec.title: Errors by model and status
spec.description: Errors concentrated on one model are a different problem from errors spread across all of them.

spec.title: Transport events
spec.description: WebSocket-level events - connection open, close, error. A close-code storm here explains latency and error spikes that look inexplicable at the response layer.

spec.title: Safety buffering events
spec.description: The provider held the stream back for a safety check. Directly visible to the user as a stall, and invisible in every latency histogram that measures the engine rather than the stream.

spec.title: Error records
spec.description: Full error records including error_message and error_code, with the thread and turn ids needed to find what the user was doing at the time.

spec.title: Transport records
spec.description: Individual transport frames with transport_event and frame_type.

options.content:
Nine record types reach Loki: **turn, message, agent_message, prompt, instructions, tool_call, tool_output, error, transport**. Only three fields are stream
**labels** (`service_name`, `codexlb_family`, `codexlb_record_type`) - everything else rides as
**structured metadata**, which is queryable without opening a new stream per value. That split is the
entire reason this pipeline pushes to Loki natively instead of using OTLP logs.

Lines older than `loki.max_line_age` (3h) are dropped **here**, deliberately, rather than being handed
to Loki to discard silently behind a 204. Catching up on a backlog therefore produces a
`too_old` rejection count on the Pipeline tab and a gap here - that is the design working, not a fault.

spec.title: Record volume by type
spec.description: All nine types stacked. Ratios between them are stable in normal operation, so a change in shape is a change in how the agent is being used.

spec.title: Record volume by family
spec.description: websocket vs unknown. A rising unknown share means frames are arriving in a shape the classifier does not recognise - worth investigating before it becomes a silent gap.

spec.title: User prompts
spec.description: What was actually asked. Carries the same thread/session/window metadata as everything else, so any line here pivots straight into the matching turn.

spec.title: Messages
spec.description: Conversation messages carrying full token accounting per line.

spec.title: All records, live
spec.description: Everything, filtered by the tab variables. The catch-all view for when you do not yet know which record type holds the answer.

spec.title: Search all record content
spec.description: Case-insensitive regex over line content, driven by the $search variable at the top. Leave it as . to match everything.

options.content:
One trace per **logical turn**. The root span is `turn`; under it sit the critical-path
children - `critical_path.pre_inference`, `critical_path.engine_wall`,
`critical_path.sampling_and_stream` and `critical_path.other` - plus a
`generateText`/`streamText <model>` span per model call and an
`execute_tool <tool>` span per tool
invocation. Span names follow the OTel GenAI convention of `<operation> <target>`, so the model and
tool name are in the span name as well as in attributes.

The same decomposition appears as histograms on the **Latency** tab. Use these when you need one
specific slow turn; use the histograms when you need the shape across all of them.

spec.title: Slowest turns
spec.description: Root spans over 30 seconds. Click a trace id to open the waterfall and see which critical-path child owns the time.

spec.title: Recent turns
spec.description: Every logical turn as a trace, newest first.

spec.title: Tool execution spans
spec.description: One span per tool call, carrying the bounded arguments. The 16KB bound is applied at a rune boundary, so a truncated argument is still valid UTF-8.

spec.title: Model call spans
spec.description: The inference spans. Span name is `<operation> <model>`, so the model is greppable without opening the span, and the operation says whether the response streamed. Named generateText/streamText rather than the GenAI convention's `chat` because that is the vocabulary Grafana agent observability recognises - see attr's GenAIOperationGenerateText (#32).

spec.title: Critical path spans
spec.description: The stage spans on their own, for when you want to compare one stage across many turns rather than all stages within one turn.

spec.title: Errored turns
spec.description: Traces whose root span carries error status. Empty is the expected state.

spec.title: This tab is about the exporter, not the agent

options.content:
Everything on the other tabs describes codex-lb's traffic. This tab describes **codexlb2otel itself** -
whether it is keeping up, whether it is losing data, and whether its sinks are accepting what it sends.

**Ingest lag is the metric that catches every other failure first.** It is the only wall-clock
subtraction in the pipeline; all other timing is measured against the archive's own clock so that
catching up on a backlog does not look like an outage.

One trap worth stating: `files_reclaimed` staying flat while retention is enabled means deletion is
**failing**, not that nothing was due - a read-only archive mount returns EROFS on every attempt.

spec.title: Ingest lag
spec.description: Sustained growth means the tailer is falling behind the writer. Healthy is around the poll interval.

spec.title: Read throughput
spec.description: Compressed archive bytes consumed per second. Spikes on startup as the backlog is worked through, then settles to the write rate.

spec.title: Decode pipeline
spec.description: The three stages of reduction. Lines far exceeding turns is normal - many frames reduce to one turn.

spec.title: Partial member reads
spec.description: A gzip member cut off mid-write at the tail of the file. This is the NORMAL steady state of tailing a file being appended to, and a healthy rate here is the signal that ingestion is keeping up. Deliberately never conflated with decode errors below.

spec.title: Data faults
spec.description: A complete-but-corrupt gzip member, or a line that would not parse. Unlike partial reads above, these are real faults: counted, dropped, and the checkpoint moves past them so one bad byte cannot wedge the pipeline.

spec.title: Archive files
spec.description: Watched should track the retention window. Replacements count a file recreated at the same name as different content - real behaviour, caught by fingerprinting the head rather than trusting the path.

spec.title: Current file offset
spec.description: How far into the live archive file the checkpoint has advanced. Sawtooth as each hour's file rolls over.

spec.title: Reducer state
spec.description: Open responses growing without bound means completion frames are not arriving. Persisted series and threads are never pruned by design, so slow growth is expected and fast growth is not. Evictions are in-flight responses given up on - measured against the archive's watermark, not the wall clock, so a backlog does not evict everything on the first pass.

spec.title: Sink backlog
spec.description: Lines buffered and not yet pushed, per sink. Should hover near zero and return to it.

spec.title: Sink rejections (rate)
spec.description: Deliveries refused, BY REASON - the reason matters far more than the count. too_old is the Loki max_line_age guard dropping backlog locally rather than letting Loki discard it behind a 204, and is expected while catching up. unauthorized or bad_request is a config fault that will NOT fix itself and holds the checkpoint until someone intervenes.

spec.title: Sink rejections in range (cumulative)
spec.description: The rate panel goes flat once rejections STOP, which reads identically to never having had any. This one keeps the count visible after the fact, which is what you actually want when asking 'did we lose anything today?'. A cumulative counter, so read it as a total rather than a rate.

spec.title: Exporter log stream
spec.description: codexlb2otel's OWN stdout, collected by the docker integration - a different stream from the conversation records it pushes. This is where a flush failure or a config fault says so in words.
